title_en: Guangzhou Zhujiang Copper Factory Co., Ltd. v. Foshan Nanhai Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Factory and Li Liefen — dispute over processing contract
ruling_gist_en: Where the parties have a dispute over the understanding of a contract term, the true meaning of the term shall be determined in accordance with the words and expressions used in the contract, the relevant provisions of the contract, the purpose of the contract, trade practices, and the principle of good faith. A contract is entered into by the parties based on actual transactional needs, and under specific circumstances, the parties will make specific expressions of intent. As long as such expressions of intent are genuine and do not violate mandatory or prohibitive provisions of the law, they shall be protected.

full_text_en:
Guangzhou Zhujiang Copper Factory Co., Ltd. v. Foshan Nanhai District Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant and Li Liefen — dispute over processing contract

Ruling Summary

Where the parties disagree on the interpretation of a contract clause, the true intention of that clause shall be determined in accordance with the words and expressions used in the contract, the relevant clauses of the contract, the purpose of the contract, the trade usage, and the principle of good faith. Where the parties enter into a contract based on actual transactional needs, they may express a specific intention under specific conditions. As long as such expression of intention is genuine and does not violate mandatory or prohibitive provisions of the law, it shall be protected.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 153

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Foshan Nanhai District Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant, domiciled at Hefeng Village Committee Hefeng Village Group, Heshun Town, Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Liefen, Chairman of the Company.

Agents ad litem: Li Bo, lawyer from Beijing Tianping Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Qiao Zhaoshu, lawyer from Beijing Tianping Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guangzhou Zhujiang Copper Factory Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 17, Industry Avenue, High-tech Industrial Park, Conghua City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xie Mingyun, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: He Wei, lawyer from Guangdong Guoding Law Firm.

Appellee at Second Instance (Defendant at First Instance): Li Liefen, male, Han ethnicity, born on June 8, 1945, domiciled in Nanhai District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Bo, lawyer from Beijing Tianping Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Qiao Zhaoshu, lawyer from Beijing Tianping Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Foshan Nanhai District Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant (hereinafter referred to as Zhongxing Smelting Plant), dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2011) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 23 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the dispute over a processing contract with the respondent, Guangzhou Zhujiang Copper Factory Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhu Copper Company), and the appellee at second instance, Li Liefen, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by Civil Ruling (2011) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 328 dated July 12, 2012, decided to bring this case for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on October 11, 2012. The agents ad litem of Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen, Li Bo and Qiao Zhaoshu, and the agent ad litem of Zhu Copper Company, He Wei, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

On May 9, 2005, Zhu Copper Company filed a lawsuit with the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, alleging that Li Liefen had entered into processing contracts with Zhu Copper Company in 1999 and 2000, which were stamped with the official seal of "Nanhai Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant." The contracts stipulated that Zhu Copper Company would provide reverberatory furnace slag to Zhongxing Smelting Plant for processing, and Zhongxing Smelting Plant would return copper ingots with a copper content of not less than 84% to Zhu Copper Company. However, Zhongxing Smelting Plant never fully returned the copper ingots as agreed in the contracts. On May 19, 2003, Zhu Copper Company and Zhongxing Smelting Plant entered into a supplementary agreement, negotiating to increase the copper recovery rate to 27%, and confirming that, calculated at the new recovery rate, Zhongxing Smelting Plant owed Zhu Copper Company a total of 943.52 tons of copper ingots, equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper. Zhongxing Smelting Plant is a sole proprietorship invested in and established by Li Liefen, registered on February 9, 2001. Neither Zhongxing Smelting Plant nor Li Liefen were shareholders of Jilin Changbai Economic Development Zone Changshun Nonferrous Metal Processing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changshun Company) or the Korean Hye-san Youth Cooperative Project. Zhu Copper Company requested the court to: 1. Order Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen to deliver the owed copper ingots with a copper content of 84%, totaling 943.52 tons (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper), or to compensate RMB 10,682,460.65 plus interest from the date of filing the lawsuit until the date of full payment (calculated at the corresponding loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China). 2. Bear the case acceptance fee and preservation fee.

Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen responded in defense, arguing that Zhu Copper Company's claims were unfounded. 1. Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen had performed their obligations under the processing contracts, and there was no outstanding copper debt. 2. There had been no amendment to the original processing contract between Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Zhu Copper Company; the purpose of the contract had been achieved, and the original contract had been terminated. According to the agreement between the parties, repayment was conditional on the profitability of Changshun Company, a cooperative entity of Zhu Copper Company's superior unit. The cooperation with Changshun Company was halted due to reasons attributable to Zhu Copper Company's superior unit, making it impossible for Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen to perform the agreement. 3. After the processing contract had been fully performed and terminated, the parties, in the form of a supplementary agreement, agreed to increase the recovery rate from 21% to 27% for copper ingots that had already been processed. However, this clause was not an amendment to the original contract but was for a new purpose, namely the Changshun Company project, which both parties clearly understood. 4. The agreement between the parties that "Party B owes Party A 792.56 tons of metallic copper, which can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the successful operation and profitability of the Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smeltery and the Korean Hye-san Youth Copper Mine Cooperation Project" was a conditional civil juristic act, not an agreement on the method of repaying the copper debt. The civil juristic act of Zhongxing Smelting Plant returning 943.52 tons of copper ingots was not an obligation under the original contract; therefore, the aforementioned agreement was not an agreement on the method of performing an obligation. Since the Changshun Company and its Korean Hye-san Youth Copper Mine Cooperation Project were not successful and had no profits, the civil juristic act of Zhongxing Smelting Plant returning 943.52 tons of copper ingots did not take effect according to law, and Zhongxing Smelting Plant was not legally obligated to repay the outstanding copper debt. Therefore, they requested the rejection of Zhu Copper Company's claims.

The court of first instance found through trial that: Zhu Copper Company and Zhongxing Smelting Plant entered into a processing contract on January 26, 1999, and another on January 26, 2000. The processing contract dated January 26, 1999, stipulated: "Quantity of reverberatory furnace slag: 5,000 tons; yield rate: 21%; processing fee: RMB 500 per ton. Processing period: from January 26, 1999, to the last furnace at the end of 1999. Settlement method: Upon quarterly return of qualified copper ingots, Zhu Copper Company will pay the processing fee. Quality: Return copper ingots with a copper content of 84%, accepted after inspection according to Zhu Copper Company general warehouse acceptance standards." The processing contract dated January 26, 2000, stipulated: "Quantity of reverberatory furnace slag: 5,000 tons; yield rate: 21%; processing fee: RMB 500 per ton. Processing period: from January 26, 2000, to the last furnace at the end of 2000. Settlement method: Upon quarterly return of qualified copper ingots, Zhu Copper Company will pay the processing fee. Quality: Return copper ingots with a copper content of 84%, payment made after acceptance according to Zhu Copper Company general warehouse acceptance standards." During the first instance proceedings, both parties confirmed that the copper yield rate under the contract dated January 26, 2000, was 21%, and both acknowledged that the processing fees under both contracts had been paid. However, Zhu Copper Company claimed that the processing fees were actually prepaid, and it usually prepaid the processing fee based on the amount of copper slag; Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen claimed that they strictly performed the contracts and received the processing fees only after delivering the copper ingots.

On April 10, 1999, Zhu Copper Company, as Party A, and Zhongxing Smelting Plant, as Party B, entered into a supplementary contract, stipulating: "In order to expedite the construction progress of the Changshun Company project and to bring it into operation as soon as possible, Party A now entrusts Party B with the processing of reverberatory furnace copper slag. Originally, the copper content in the slag to be returned was set at 27%. The 21% return rate stipulated in the current processing contract is a provisional figure. Party A agrees that the shortfall shall be returned by Party B to Party A from Party B's future profits in Changshun Company."

In May 2001, Zhu Copper Company, as Party A, and Zhongxing Smelting Plant, as Party B, entered into an agreement, stipulating: "Party A entrusts Party B with the processing of miscellaneous copper ingots. According to the original contract, the outstanding portion of the miscellaneous copper ingots to be returned by Party B to Party A totals 943.524 tons. Party B agrees to repay this amount in full in the future." Li Liefen signed this agreement and noted: "The copper thus owed can only be repaid from profits of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smeltery when it becomes profitable."

On May 19, 2003, Zhu Copper Company, as Party A, and Zhongxing Smelting Plant, as Party B, entered into a supplementary agreement, stipulating: "In 1999 and 2000, Party A entrusted Party B with the processing of miscellaneous copper ingots. The contract stipulated that the return rate of miscellaneous copper ingots (containing 84% copper) by Party B was 21%. In May 2001, the parties jointly discussed and increased the original recovery rate of 21% to a recovery rate of 27%. Calculated at the new recovery rate, Party B owes Party A a total of 943.52 tons of miscellaneous copper ingots (containing 84% copper) (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper). The 792.56 tons of metallic copper owed by Party B to Party A can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the successful operation and profitability of the Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smeltery and the Korean Hye-san Youth Copper Mine Cooperation Project."

The court of first instance further found that the predecessor of Zhongxing Smelting Plant was the "Nanhai County Heshun Hefeng Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant," a sole proprietorship established by Li Liefen in 1986. In 1988, with the approval of the industry and commerce administrative department, it was changed from an individual enterprise to a collectively-owned enterprise (in fact, it was operated by Li Liefen individually under the name of a collective enterprise). In September 1993, the enterprise name was changed to "Nanhai Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant." In December 1996, "Nanhai Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant" was changed from collectively-owned to a private enterprise with the approval of the industry and commerce administrative department, and the relevant license renewal procedures were completed. In February 2004, the enterprise name was changed to "Foshan Nanhai District Zhongxing Hardware Smelting Plant." Thus, Zhongxing Smelting Plant is a sole proprietorship invested in and established by Li Liefen.

"Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smeltery" was a joint venture company to be established under the "Jilin Changshun Nonferrous Metal Processing Co., Ltd. Articles of Association" formulated on January 6, 1999, by Guangzhou Metallurgical Group Guangzhou Copper Factory (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Copper Factory), Nanhai Guangshunda Copper Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangshunda Company), and Jilin Changbai County Transportation Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changbai Transportation Company). This company was actually established, with its full name being "Jilin Changbai Economic Development Zone Changshun Nonferrous Metal Processing Co., Ltd.," and its business license was revoked by the industry and commerce administrative department on July 21, 2004.

"Korean Hye-san Youth Copper Mine" was a joint venture company to be established under the "China-Korea Huigui Joint Venture Contract" signed on March 14, 2003, between Hye-san Youth Mine of the Korean Ryanggang Province Mining Enterprise Association and China Guangzhou Nonferrous Metals Group Co., Ltd.

Guangzhou Nonferrous Metals Group Co., Ltd. is the supervisory authority of Guangzhou Copper Factory and also its investor. Zhu Copper Company is a Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise established by Guangzhou Copper Factory, meaning Guangzhou Copper Factory is the parent company of Zhu Copper Company.

Guangshunda Company is a Sino-foreign joint venture invested in and established by Zhongxing Smelting Plant, Guangzhou Copper Factory, and Hong Kong Ruheng Development Co., Ltd., approved for establishment on February 13, 1992. Its current shareholders are Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Hong Kong Dade Trading Co., Ltd. Its legal representative has always been Li Liefen, and its current name is "Foshan Nanhai District Guangshunda Copper Materials Co., Ltd."

The court of first instance further found that regarding the nature of the cooperative project mentioned in the supplementary agreement dated May 19, 2003, Zhu Copper Company, Zhongxing Smelting Plant, and Li Liefen gave inconsistent accounts. Zhu Copper Company asserted that the cooperative project was a project between Guangzhou Nonferrous Metals Group Co., Ltd. and Hye-san Youth Mine of the Korean Ryanggang Province Mining Enterprise Association to jointly develop the youth mine, located in North Korea, and that the purpose of the cooperation was to mine the youth mine. It stated that the project was terminated on its own because the state did not approve it. Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen asserted that the cooperative project was the establishment of Changshun Company by Guangzhou Copper Factory, Guangshunda Company, and Changbai Transportation Company, and then the purchase of raw materials from the Korean Hye-san Youth Copper Mine for processing by Changshun Company. Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen did not dispute that the cooperative project had not been formally put into operation and had no profits, but argued that the failure of the project to be successfully brought into operation was caused by the parent company of Zhu Copper Company.

The court of first instance held that the processing contract, supplementary contract, agreement, and supplementary agreement involved in this case, entered into between Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Zhu Copper Company, were all true expressions of the parties' intentions, and their contents did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and were therefore lawfully effective. Zhu Copper Company requested Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen to return the outstanding copper of 943.52 tons (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper) or to compensate for the corresponding economic losses. Therefore, this case must first determine the following basic facts: 1. The reason for the formation of the disputed copper debt of 943.52 tons; 2. Whether the parties agreed on repayment conditions or repayment methods for this copper debt in their agreements, and whether, under the circumstance that the agreed repayment conditions or repayment methods cannot be realized, Zhongxing Smelting Plant and Li Liefen are still obligated to repay the disputed copper.

For the cause of formation of the disputed debt of 943.52 tons of copper, both parties held different views. Zhutong Company claimed that the debt arose in the course of performing the "Processing Contracts" concluded in 1999 and 2000, and was a summary of the copper owed by Zhongxing Smelter in those two years. Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen argued that the disputed debt was not formed historically, but was a debt created for the purpose of achieving a new cooperative goal by increasing the copper ingot recovery rate through agreement. The court of first instance held that the claims of Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen were more consistent with legal truth. The reasons are as follows:

First, as to the amount of 943.52 tons of impure copper ingots (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper) stated in two agreements dated May 2001 and May 19, 2003, Zhutong Company consistently maintained that this was the summary of copper owed by Zhongxing Smelter in 1999 and 2000, calculated at a copper recovery rate of 27% after reconciliation. However, at the second hearing of the first instance, Zhutong Company changed its position, stating that the summary was calculated at a recovery rate of 21%, and that the "Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" were entered into only to confirm the amount of copper owed and to interrupt the statute of limitations, without verifying whether the calculation was based on a 21% or 27% recovery rate. This statement was contradictory. The calculation of the disputed debt of 943.52 tons is a key fact in the case. As a party that personally experienced the execution of the agreements and was fully aware of the facts, Zhutong Company's statement on this key fact was so inconsistent that it reasonably raised doubts. The exclusion of reasonable doubt is a necessary requirement for the formation of a judge's inner conviction in civil proceedings. Given that such reasonable doubt could not be eliminated, the claimant Zhutong Company had failed to meet its burden of proof.

Second, from the literal meaning of the "Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement," the disputed debt was calculated at a copper recovery rate of 27%. Zhutong Company's current claim that it was calculated at 21% is inconsistent with the content of the agreements.

Third, during the performance of the "Processing Contract" dated January 26, 1999, the parties entered into a "Supplementary Contract" on April 10 of the same year, stipulating that the part of the copper owed "Party A agrees that Party B shall return to Party A from Party B's profits in Changshun Company in the future." In other words, before the performance of the contract concluded in 1999 was completed, and while it was still uncertain whether Zhongxing Smelter had fulfilled its obligation to return copper ingots as agreed, the parties had already predetermined the content of the copper debt. Combined with the context of the contract, the so-called "part owed" referred to the difference between the amount of copper to be returned calculated at the originally stipulated copper recovery rate of 27% for copper slag and the amount calculated at the 21% recovery rate stipulated in the current "Processing Contract." Taking into account the similarity in wording and the coherent and continuing content of the "Supplementary Contract," the "Agreement," and the "Supplementary Agreement," in the absence of contrary evidence, it can be inferred that the disputed copper debt confirmed in the "Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement," calculated "according to the original contract provisions" and "according to the new recovery rate," also referred to the difference between the amount of copper to be returned calculated at the originally stipulated 27% copper slag recovery rate and the amount calculated at the 21% recovery rate stipulated in the current "Processing Contract."

Finally, according to the terms of the "Processing Contracts" dated January 26, 1999 and January 26, 2000, which stated "upon acceptance of quarterly returned copper ingots, Zhutong Company shall pay the processing fee" and "return copper ingots with 84% content, payment shall be made after acceptance in accordance with the acceptance standards of Zhutong's general warehouse," and the fact that both parties acknowledged during the proceedings that Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen had received the processing fees, it can generally be inferred that Zhongxing Smelter had returned copper ingots conforming to the contract. Since neither party was able to provide the key evidence of the quantity of copper ingots delivered by Zhongxing Smelter to Zhutong Company in 1999 and 2000, it is difficult to determine, based solely on the defective evidence provided by both parties, the specific quantities of copper slag and copper ingots returned and processing fees paid in 1999 and 2000, nor is it easy to overturn the above inference. Zhutong Company's claim that Zhongxing Smelter did not fully perform its obligation to return copper and that the processing fees paid were in fact prepayments is inconsistent with the contract and lacks sufficient evidence.

During the proceedings, Zhutong Company submitted 12 material release forms for outsourced processing and 30 special VAT invoices, seeking to show that the amount of copper returned by Zhongxing Smelter was insufficient. Calculated at a 21% recovery rate, the shortfall was 935.898 tons, which is roughly consistent with the debt confirmed in the agreement. However, the probative value of the evidence adduced by Zhutong Company was clearly lacking. For example, of the 12 material release forms, only one recorded the actual quantity of reverberatory furnace slag issued; the remaining 11 only recorded the estimated quantity, with the actual quantity column left blank, thus failing to reflect the actual amount of reverberatory furnace slag supplied to Zhongxing Smelter. The VAT invoices were all dated July 14, 2000, and thus could not reflect the dates and amounts of the actual processing fees paid in 1999 and 2000. Moreover, from the invoice numbers, they should have been issued consecutively, but the evidence submitted by Zhutong Company showed missing numbers, which Zhutong Company could not further explain. If, as Zhutong Company claimed, the processing fees paid were actually prepayments and the company usually prepaid processing fees based on the amount of copper slag, then based on the total copper slag of 10,373.905 tons reflected in the 12 material release forms, the prepaid processing fees should have been RMB 5,186,952.50. This is clearly inconsistent with the total processing fee of RMB 2,958,627.50 reflected in the 30 VAT invoices. Moreover, if Zhutong Company had indeed prepaid such a large amount of processing fees and Zhongxing Smelter had not fully performed its obligation to return copper, it would be unreasonable for Zhutong Company not to claim any loss from the overpayment from Zhongxing Smelter over several years. Therefore, the evidence adduced by Zhutong Company lacked sufficient probative value, and the conclusion drawn from it lacked a sufficient factual basis.

It follows that the claim of Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen, that the disputed debt of 943.52 tons of copper was not historically formed but was a separate debt created for the purpose of achieving a new cooperative goal by increasing the copper ingot recovery rate through agreement, is more consistent with the legal facts reflected by the available evidence. Therefore, in accordance with Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 63 and 72 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the court of first instance adopted this claim and confirmed that the disputed copper debt is the difference between the amount of copper to be returned calculated at the 27% copper slag recovery rate and the amount calculated at the 21% recovery rate.

Regarding whether Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen still need to repay the disputed copper debt if the repayment conditions or methods agreed upon in the agreements cannot be realized. As stated above, the disputed copper debt was not historically formed but was a separate debt created outside the "Processing Contracts" by means of an agreement to increase the copper ingot recovery rate for the purpose of achieving a new cooperative goal. Therefore, combined with the fact that all three agreements related to the debt in question include the content that the debt can only be repaid from the profits of the shareholding in the Changshun Company project, it should be determined that this is an agreement on the repayment conditions for the debt, as this interpretation is more consistent with the purpose of the relevant contracts and their literal meaning. If, as Zhutong Company claims, the agreement that the debt can only be repaid from the profits of the shareholding in the Changshun Company project is an agreement on the method of repaying the copper, then it would be clearly unreasonable for the parties to repeatedly emphasize this as the sole method of repayment while it was still uncertain whether the Changshun Company project would generate any profit.

As to the content of the cooperative project, the parties also held different views. However, based on the process of signing and the content of the "Supplementary Contract," the "Agreement," and the "Supplementary Agreement," and in light of evidence such as the "Contract for the Joint Venture to Establish Jilin Changshun Nonferrous Metal Processing Co., Ltd." and the articles of association of Changshun Company, it can be seen that Zhutong Company and Zhongxing Smelter were clear about the relationships among the various parties in the project and that the "cooperative project" referred to in the agreements meant Changshun Company. Moreover, Zhutong Company was also clear that the "Party B" in the agreements actually referred to Guangshunda Company. If Zhutong Company were not clear about this, it would not have repeatedly entered into agreements stipulating that the debt would be repaid from the profits available to Zhongxing Smelter or Li Liefen in Changshun Company. Therefore, the "cooperative project" in the agreements first referred to Li Liefen's establishment of Changshun Company in the name of Guangshunda Company with the parent company of Zhutong Company and the Jilin side, and then the purchase of raw materials from the Korean Huishan Youth Copper Mine for processing by Changshun Company. Zhutong Company argued that it was unaware of the composition of the cooperative project parties when it signed the agreements, claiming it was an independent entity from its parent company and that it had previously been misled by Li Liefen, and that it only learned before the lawsuit that Zhongxing Smelter or Li Liefen held no shares in the cooperative project. The court of first instance held that this claim was untenable. From the available evidence, such as the "Sino-Korean Huiguang Joint Venture Contract," the "Contract for the Joint Venture to Establish Jilin Changshun Nonferrous Metal Processing Co., Ltd.," and the articles of association of Changshun Company, it can be seen that the original legal representative of Zhutong Company, Liang Xiru, had signed the cooperative project agreement at that time as an authorized representative of the parent company, Guangzhou Copper Factory, and the competent authority, Guangzhou Nonferrous Metals Group Company. Moreover, Zhutong Company, during the proceedings, failed to give a clear answer to the court's repeated inquiries on this issue, stating that it could not confirm. Therefore, Zhutong Company's claim of ignorance is untenable.

From the content of the "Supplementary Agreement" dated May 19, 2003, which states: "Party B owes Party A 792.56 tons of metallic copper, which can only be repaid from the profits of Party B's shareholding after the cooperative project between Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Korean Huishan Youth Copper Mine is successfully put into operation and generates profit," the condition attached by the parties here is a suspensive condition, i.e., a condition that limits the effectiveness of a civil juristic act, so that the legal act only takes effect when the agreed fact occurs. If the condition is fulfilled, the civil juristic act takes effect, and Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen shall be liable to repay the debt of metallic copper owed. If the condition is not fulfilled or can no longer be fulfilled, the civil juristic act will definitively not take effect, and Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen are not required to perform their payment obligation. In this case, both parties acknowledged that the cooperative project had no profit, and Zhutong Company even admitted that the project was terminated on its own because the state did not approve it. This shows that the condition for returning copper and making payment attached in this case could no longer be fulfilled, and there is no evidence that the non-fulfillment of the condition was caused by the intentional conduct of Zhongxing Smelter or Li Liefen. Therefore, Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen are not required to repay the metallic copper or the corresponding amounts owed under the agreements to Zhutong Company.

In summary, Zhutong Company's claim for the return of the disputed copper ingots and compensation for corresponding losses lacked sufficient grounds, and the court of first instance did not support it. In accordance with Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: Zhutong Company's claims were dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 63,422 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 68,422, were to be borne by Zhutong Company.

Zhutong Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court, arguing: (1) The debt of 943.52 tons of copper agreed upon in the agreements should be the original debt incurred from the performance of the original contracts, and the court of first instance erred in finding it to be a newly created debt. (2) The agreement in the contracts regarding repayment from the profits of the Changshun project should be a method of repaying the copper debt, and the court of first instance erred in finding it to be a repayment condition. Zhutong Company agreed that Party B (Li Liefen) could repay from the profits of the future cooperative company; this was merely an agreement to postpone repayment, a grace period for the performance of the debt, and could not be interpreted as an intention to forgive the debt or render it unnecessary to repay. The parties did not explicitly agree on how to handle the copper debt if the project could not be put into operation and generate profit. In such a case, pursuant to Articles 61 and 62 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Contract Law"), where the method of performance is unclear, it does not mean that the copper debt is extinguished; rather, the debtor should perform in another manner. (3) The court of first instance incorrectly allocated the burden of proof, finding that Zhutong Company's evidence was insufficient and directly adopting the opinion that the copper debt was a newly added debt. Therefore, Zhutong Company requested: 1. To set aside the civil judgment (2010) Fozhong Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 1 of the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province; 2. To order Li Liefen and Zhongxing Smelter to jointly deliver the overdue 943.52 tons of copper ingots with 84% copper content (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper), or to compensate RMB 10,682,460.65 plus interest from the date of filing the lawsuit until the date of full payment (calculated at the same-period loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China); 3. To have Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen bear all litigation costs of this case.

Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen responded, arguing: (1) The three "Processing Contracts" on which this case is based were fully performed in accordance with the agreed terms, the purpose of the contracts was achieved, and the contracts were terminated. There was no fact of Zhongxing Smelter owing copper, and the judgment of first instance correctly found this. (2) Although the parties entered into a clause in the name of a "supplementary agreement" to increase the recovery rate of the already processed copper ingots from 21% to 27%, this clause was not a modification of the original contract but was intended for a new purpose: the Changshun Company project. The agreement that "Party B owes Party A 792.56 tons of metallic copper, which can only be repaid from the profits of Party B's shareholding after the cooperative project between Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Korean Huishan Youth Copper Mine is successfully put into operation and generates profit" constitutes a conditional civil juristic act, not an agreement on the method of repaying the copper debt. (3) The court of first instance correctly applied Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, finding that Zhutong Company's lawsuit lacked evidentiary support and should be dismissed. They requested that Zhutong Company's appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld.

The facts found by the Guangdong High People's Court upon retrial were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that a processing contract relationship was established between the parties. The "Processing Contracts," "Supplementary Contract," "Agreement," and "Supplementary Agreement" entered into by the parties were all the true expressions of the parties' intent, their contents did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and they should be confirmed as validly concluded. The contents of the above contracts or agreements were consistent, the claims and debts were clearly and unambiguously stated, and the amounts were specific. In particular, the "Agreement" entered into in May 2001 between Zhutong Company as Party A and Zhongxing Smelter as Party B expressly stipulated: "Party A entrusts Party B to process impure copper ingots. In accordance with the original contract provisions, the outstanding part of the impure copper ingots that Party B should return to Party A totals 943.524 tons. Party B agrees to repay all of this in the future." Li Liefen signed the agreement and noted: "The copper owed can only be repaid from the profits of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter." The "Supplementary Agreement" entered into on May 19, 2003, also expressly stipulated: "In 1999 and 2000, the contract for Party A entrusting Party B to process impure copper ingots stipulated that Party B's return of impure copper ingots (containing 84% copper) was 21%. In May 2001, Parties A and B jointly discussed and increased the original 21% recovery rate to 27%. Calculated at the new recovery rate, Party B owes Party A a total of 943.52 tons of impure copper ingots (containing 84% copper) (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper). The 792.56 tons of metallic copper owed by Party B to Party A can only be repaid from the profits of Party B's shareholding after the cooperative project between Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Korean Huishan Youth Copper Mine is successfully put into operation and generates profit." The above agreements clearly show that Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen acknowledged the debt owed to Zhutong Company and had no objection to the amount of the debt. They merely put forward a different proposal regarding the method of repayment, but this cannot negate the establishment of the claim and debt between the parties, nor can the debtor's civil liability be exempted simply because it proposed a different method of repaying the debt.

According to the agreement entered into in 1999 between Zhutong Company and Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen, Zhutong Company agreed that Party B (Li Liefen) could repay from the profits of the future cooperative company. This shows that Zhutong Company agreed to allow Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen to adopt a deferred method of repaying the debt, which was a grace period for the performance of the debt. There was no agreement between the creditor and the debtor to forgive the debt. The parties did not explicitly agree on how to handle the copper debt if the cooperative project in Korea could not be put into operation and generate profit. In such a case, pursuant to Article 61 and Article 62, Item (5) of the Contract Law, where the method of performance of a debt is unclear, it does not mean that the copper debt is extinguished; rather, the debtor should perform the debt in a manner conducive to achieving the purpose of the contract. Therefore, the claims and debts between the parties are clear, the amounts are unambiguous, and the debtor should perform the debt. Where it is unable to repay the outstanding 943.524 tons of impure copper ingots (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper), it should compensate Zhutong Company in money at the market price at the relevant time. The court of first instance found the facts clearly but erred in the application of law and incorrectly determined the liability. The judgment should be set aside. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of second instance rendered the following judgment: 1. To set aside the civil judgment (2010) Fozhong Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 1 of the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, and to amend the judgment to order Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen to jointly repay to Zhutong Company 943.524 tons of impure copper ingots (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper), or to compensate Zhutong Company RMB 10,682,460.65 plus interest thereon (from May 9, 2005 until the date of full payment, calculated at the same-period and same-type loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China). 2. The case acceptance fees of the first and second instances, totaling RMB 126,844, and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, shall all be borne by Zhongxing Smelter and Li Liefen.

Zhongxing Smelter Plant, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an application for retrial with this court, alleging: (1) The main facts found in the judgment of second instance lacked evidentiary support. 1. The three Processing Contracts signed by the parties had been fully performed in accordance with the agreed terms, the purpose of the contracts had been achieved, the contracts had been terminated, and there was no fact that Zhongxing Smelter Plant owed copper. 2. Although the parties signed, in the name of a Supplementary Agreement, a clause increasing the recovery rate from 21% to 27% for the copper ingots that had already been processed, this clause was not a modification of the original contracts but was for a new purpose, namely, the Changshun Company project. Both parties were clearly aware of this. 3. The parties' agreement that "Party B's debt to Party A of 792.56 tons of metallic copper can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable" was a conditional civil juristic act, not an agreement on the method of repaying the copper debt. The condition attached by the parties had not yet occurred, and whether it would occur in the future was objectively uncertain; it was a restriction voluntarily imposed by the parties on the civil juristic act. The attached condition did not violate mandatory legal norms, did not violate public interests or social morality; and there was no evidence to prove that Zhongxing Smelter Plant had committed fraud. Therefore, Zhongxing Smelter Plant's restriction on the validity of the civil juristic act regarding the debt of 943.52 tons of copper ingots (containing 84% copper) was lawful. (2) The judgment of second instance erred in fact-finding, leading to erroneous application of law. The judgment of second instance misinterpreted the condition attached in the agreement for repaying the copper debt. Since repaying the copper debt was not Zhongxing Smelter Plant's obligation under the original contracts but a conditional juristic act, and the attached condition had not been fulfilled, no legal effect arose, and Zhongxing Smelter Plant did not bear corresponding liability. According to Article 62 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC: "A civil juristic act may have conditions attached to it. Conditional civil juristic acts take effect when the attached conditions are satisfied." In this case, it should be determined that the conditions agreed by the parties were not fulfilled, the conditional civil juristic act did not take effect, and Zhongxing Smelter Plant bore no liability. Therefore, the claim of Zhutong Company should be dismissed.

Zhutong Company argued in response: (1) The 943.52 tons of copper debt agreed in the parties' agreement should be the original debt arising from the performance of the original contracts, not a newly created debt. (2) The agreement in the supplementary agreement regarding repayment from profits of the Changshun project should be a method of repaying the copper debt. Zhutong Company's consent that the debtor (Li Liefen) could repay from future profits of the cooperative company was merely an agreement to allow a deferred method of repayment, a grace period for debt performance, and could not be construed as meaning or indicating debt forgiveness or exemption from repayment. The parties did not clearly agree on how to handle the copper debt if the project could not commence production and become profitable. Therefore, pursuant to Articles 61 and 62 of the Contract Law, if the method of performance is not clearly agreed, it does not mean the copper debt is extinguished; rather, the debtor should perform using other methods. The court of second instance found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. The retrial application of Zhongxing Smelter Plant should be dismissed.

The facts found by this court upon retrial are the same as those found by the courts of first and second instance.

This court is of the opinion that the focus of dispute between the parties in this retrial is: How was the debt of 943.52 tons of copper owed by Zhongxing Smelter Plant formed; and whether Zhongxing Smelter Plant and Li Liefen should repay Zhutong Company a total of 943.52 tons of purple miscellaneous copper ingots (containing 84% copper) (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper).

Regarding how the debt of 943.52 tons of copper owed by Zhongxing Smelter Plant was formed. Zhutong Company argued that the disputed debt of 943.52 tons of copper was originally formed based on the Processing Contracts between the parties and was a summary of Zhongxing Smelter Plant's historical copper debts. Li Liefen and Zhongxing Smelter Plant argued that the 943.52 tons copper debt was not originally formed but was a debt established through a new agreement solely to achieve a new cooperative purpose. This court is of the opinion: According to the agreements in the Processing Contracts dated January 26, 1999, and January 26, 2000, between Zhutong Company and Zhongxing Smelter Plant, which stated "after the quarterly copper ingots are accepted as qualified, Zhutong Company will repay the processing fee" and "return copper ingots with 84% content, payment shall be made after acceptance according to Zhutong's general warehouse acceptance standards," and the fact that both parties acknowledged in the trial of first instance that Li Liefen had received the processing fees, if Zhutong Company claimed that Li Liefen had not fully performed all obligations under the said contracts, i.e., that after Zhutong Company had provided the corresponding copper slag, Li Liefen did not return the purple miscellaneous copper ingots with 84% copper content according to the agreed proportion, then Zhutong Company had the burden to prove the quantity of copper slag it had provided, the quantity of purple miscellaneous copper ingots received, and the processing fees paid to Li Liefen during the two years from 1999 to the end of 2000. However, Zhutong Company did not provide the above evidence in any of the previous trials of this case. Since the contracts stipulated that the processing fee was paid after acceptance and qualification, and the processing fees had actually been paid, the existing evidence can only prove that the contracts with a copper recovery rate of 21% as agreed by the parties had been performed. However, as for the disputed 943.52 tons of copper debt, whether it was directly calculated from the 6% difference resulting from increasing the copper recovery rate from 21% to 27%, or it was the aggregate amount of Zhongxing Smelter Plant's historical copper debts (including the portion from the 6% increase in recovery rate), both parties failed to provide a sufficiently reasonable explanation for the true cause of the copper debt or to provide specific calculation methods and factual basis. Based on the content of the contracts signed by the parties in this case, this debt includes both the debt formed by increasing the recovery rate from 21% to 27% for processing 10,000 tons of copper slag as agreed in the contracts, and the debt beyond the processing of 10,000 tons of copper slag as agreed in the contracts. The specific calculation is as follows: 10,000 x (27% - 21%) = 600 tons of copper debt was formed by increasing the recovery rate under the agreed processing contracts. As for the remaining 343.52 tons of copper debt, although the parties failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove the cause of its formation, both parties acknowledged the existence of this debt. This court confirms this. Given that both parties acknowledge that the debt of 943.52 tons of copper is objectively true and exists, and agreed that this debt "can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable," the parties made clear agreements on both the creation and repayment of this debt. This represents the true intention of the parties and forms the basis for the performance of the contracts.

Regarding whether Zhongxing Smelter Plant and Li Liefen should repay to Zhutong Company a total of 943.52 tons of purple miscellaneous copper ingots (containing 84% copper) (equivalent to 792.56 tons of metallic copper). This concerns the interpretation of the contract clause. That is, how should the agreement that Zhongxing Smelter Plant's 943.52 tons copper debt "can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable" be understood. This court is of the opinion: The interpretation of a contract should strictly follow the provisions of the Contract Law and the agreement of the parties. The Guangdong High People's Court, in its judgment of second instance, interpreted "can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable" as an agreement on the method of returning the copper debt, on the ground that the parties did not agree on whether Zhongxing Smelter Plant should repay the copper debt if the project failed to commence production successfully and become profitable, which was deemed unclear. This finding does not conform to the rules of contract interpretation. Because in this case, the parties only disputed the understanding of the terms of the contract clause; it was not a situation where the contract had no agreement or the agreement was unclear. Where the parties dispute the understanding of a contract clause, the true meaning of the clause shall be determined according to the words and expressions used in the contract, the relevant terms of the contract, the purpose of the contract, trade practices, and the principle of good faith. In the Supplementary Agreement dated May 19, 2003, the meaning expressed by "can only be repaid from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable" is clear. Even if "repayment from Party B's share of profits after the cooperative project of Changbai Changshun Nonferrous Metal Smelter and the Hyesan Youth Copper Mine of North Korea successfully commences production and becomes profitable" is understood as an agreement on the method of repayment, it is limited to "only this method," and no other alternative method was agreed. From the literal meaning of the contract, the agreement of "can only" specifically limits the conditions and scope for performing the copper debt. This condition is the prerequisite for Zhongxing Smelter Plant and Li Liefen to perform the copper debt they acknowledge. In this case, both parties should have been able to foresee the risks in the performance of the supplementary agreement. When parties enter into a contract based on their actual transaction needs, they will make specific expressions of intent under specific conditions according to their needs. As long as their expression of intent is genuine, does not violate prohibitive legal provisions, and there is no fraud or coercion, it should be respected and protected.

In summary, the grounds for Zhongxing Smelter Plant's application for retrial are valid, and this court supports them. Pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2011) Yue Gao Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 23 of the Guangdong High People's Court is hereby set aside;

2. The Civil Judgment (2010) Fo Zhong Fa Min Er Zhong Zi No. 1 of the Foshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province is hereby affirmed.

The case acceptance fees for first and second instance, totaling RMB 126,844, and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, shall be borne by Guangzhou Pearl River Copper Factory Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
